easy.p1: In Konta an invoice looks like an invoice. You can see straight away what needs filling in, and whatever is calculated for you stays out of the way.
easy.p2: The interface is in Romanian, Russian and English. Account names are in Romanian, and in Russian in the Russian interface, as the Romanian and Russian editions of the Ministry of Finance order give them. The terms come from the national accounting standards and the Tax Code, the way you say them every day.
easy.p3: When something goes wrong, a person answers the phone, in Romanian or Russian.

ef.caveat: Every rule here is in our public register, with a reference to the legal act. A licensed accountant is still checking the values.
ef.law.p1: Today e-Factura is mandatory in four cases: supplies to state institutions and in public procurement, supplies to agents with no fiscal relationship with the budget (since 1 January 2025), supplies for the projects named in art. 104(c¹) of the Tax Code, and companies that SFS has put on its risk list.
ef.law.p2: International VAT trackers wrote that e-Factura would become mandatory for every company on 1 October 2026. That date has passed, and as of 15 October 2026 no Moldovan legal act sets it: for every other VAT payer, e-Factura remains optional. The list of companies that must use it grows through SFS orders; the latest, Order 494 of 2 October 2026, added six companies. If an obligation for everyone is adopted, we’ll add it to the register and say so here.
ef.law.p3: From 1 January 2026 the rule that denied a buyer the VAT deduction on a paper invoice from a listed supplier was repealed.
ef.law.p4: A VAT refund is capped at a share of the VAT that buyers paid, documented through e-Factura and through cash registers connected to MEV. Government Decision 496/2025 raised that share from 20% to 70% from 14 August 2025.

ef.p1: Konta brings the electronic invoices of all your client companies onto one screen. A purchase invoice received through e-Factura becomes, on request, a draft in the books, which the accountant checks and posts. Issuing invoices from Konta comes next, so nothing has to be typed in twice.
ef.title: e-Factura for all your clients, on one screen
ef.today.p1: The e-Factura screen shows the company’s issued and received invoices, and those of every client of an accounting firm, from a copy Konta refreshes from SFS with each company’s API user; each refresh ends in the company’s trail with the calls it made. A received invoice becomes a draft purchase invoice, with the supplier found by IDNO and VAT from the rulebook. On SFS’s test service, a draft sent through Konta’s e-Factura client was signed by the director and read back, on 27 October 2026. Issuing from Konta is the next step. The client’s code is public, for anyone to read.

faq.a1: Not yet. Konta has the sales and purchase VAT registers that TVA12 is built from, but not the return’s form. We will call it done only when it matches, field by field, returns actually filed by real companies. Until then we do not say Konta does TVA12.
faq.a10: No. Neither the app nor the site loads analytics, screen-recording or any other third-party scripts. The Content Security Policy (CSP) both send lets the browser run only their own scripts. You can check this yourself in the browser’s Network tab.
faq.a2: For rates, thresholds, accounts and deadlines, yes. No rate is written into Konta’s code: it reads them from a public register in which each value carries the date it applies from and the act it comes from. Filing and payment deadlines are in the same register, each with its act and article, and the tax calendar on this site shows them month by month. A licensed accountant is still reviewing the register. In the app, each company has its own deadlines from the same register, each with an owner and a status.
faq.a3: Nobody, without the company director’s consent. When support needs to see something, it asks for access; the director grants it in the “Acces Konta” tab, read-only and for a limited time, can close it at any moment, and the access appears in the company’s audit trail. There is one exception, for emergencies: the platform owner can open access without consent, with a written reason and for at most a day. That too is recorded in the company’s trail, and the directors get an email. The database enforces these rules, not only the app.
faq.a4: The database. Every table holding client data carries the company’s identifier and is protected by PostgreSQL’s row-level security: a query sees only the rows of the companies the signed-in person has access to, even if the code forgets a filter. The app connects with a role that cannot bypass this rule, and an automated test fails if a table appears without it.
faq.a5: No. The database refuses to change or delete an entry, a posted invoice or a payment. A mistake is corrected by a reversal and a new entry, both in plain sight. Nothing enters a closed month; reopening one needs a reason and stays in the audit trail. The audit trail is a hash chain, so a row changed behind its back shows up when the chain is verified. Planned: publishing the chain’s head somewhere we cannot rewrite, so that not even we could rewrite the whole chain unnoticed.
faq.a6: Today Konta runs as a demo, at demo.konta.md, and as a preview, at app.konta.md, on servers rented from our hosting provider. The same provider holds the konta.md site and the mailboxes the app sends its mail through. Nobody else processes data: neither the app nor the site loads anything from third parties. Before the first pilot client, the app moves to a separate production server in the European Union, with backups encrypted before they leave the server and copied daily to Moldova. The Security page keeps the list current.
faq.a7: Yes. Anyone with access to a company’s books downloads them from the app after confirming who they are again: every table they have access to, as .xlsx and as JSON, with exact amounts, the bank statements as they were received, and a list of the files with their fingerprints. The export works while the organisation is suspended too, goes into the company’s trail and costs nothing.
faq.a8: We have decided this: if Konta stops, customers get at least six months’ notice, during which they can read their data and export all of it. Accounting records are kept for years, so nobody should be left without them. The guarantee goes into the terms of service before the first pilot client. It rests on the full export, which exists already.
faq.a9: No, and we will not ask for them. Konta does not keep your SFS portal password, your bank login or your electronic signature: you sign yourself. For e-Factura, Konta uses an API user that the director creates in SIA e-Factura and enters in Konta. Such a user can do anything e-Factura allows, so Konta keeps it encrypted, and every use goes into the company’s trail before it is made. Bank statements are imported from a file.

priv.basis.p1: We answer because you wrote to us: answering a message we receive is our legitimate interest, and you are expecting that answer. When you ask for a demo or an offer, the processing is a step we take at your request before a possible contract. Limiting messages by IP address protects the form from abuse, also in our legitimate interest. You can object at any time to processing based on our legitimate interest.
priv.basis.p2: The bases are those in art. 6(1)(b) and (f) of Law No. 195/2024 on personal data protection, in force since 23 August 2026.
priv.changes.p: If we change how we use data, we update this page and the date above. A change that would need new consent does not apply without it.
priv.cookies.p1: The site uses no analytics, tracking or advertising tools and loads nothing from other sites. In your browser it keeps only the language and theme you choose: the konta_lang and konta_theme cookies, with konta_lang_at and konta_theme_at recording when you chose. They are shared with app.konta.md, so the app opens in the same language and theme, and they last a year. The same two values are also kept in the browser's storage (konta.lang, konta.theme).
priv.demo.p1: When you register in the demo we keep your account (name, email address, your password only as a cryptographic fingerprint, language and theme), your answers on the form (what you will use Konta for, your role, how many companies you keep books for, which 1C you use, your phone number if you give it, the two checkboxes) and everything you enter in the app: companies, partners, documents, salaries. For security we also keep when you sign in, the IP address and browser you do it from, and which actions were taken in each company. We treat everything you type into the demo as real data, with the same protections as in the app.
priv.demo.p2: We use it so that you can use the demo, as you asked (art. 6(1)(b)); to protect it from abuse and to see which parts of the program are used, so we can improve it (our legitimate interest, (f)); and, only if you ticked “Konta may contact me about the product”, to write to you or call you about Konta (your consent, (a)). You can withdraw that consent at any time by writing to mail@konta.md.
priv.demo.p3: Konta's operators see in their console your name, email address, organisation, your answers on the form, your feedback and the days you used the demo. They do not see the companies' books, unless the company's director gives them support access, for a limited time. The demo's server is with the same hosting provider as the app.
priv.demo.p4: The demo and everything in it are deleted three months after Konta launches; the exact date will be announced in advance, and you will be told when Konta launches. The demo's encrypted backups are kept for at most 30 days and deleted at the same time. After the launch you will be able to transfer your existing data from the demo into Konta, if you wish. You can export your data at any time, in one click. For the founding offer we pass to the real app only your confirmed email address, the date it was confirmed and your choice about being contacted.
priv.demo.p5: The accounts and data that were on app.konta.md on 29 October 2026 were copied into the demo that day, so the people using them could carry on there. Since then the two are separate, and at launch app.konta.md starts empty.
priv.keep.p1: Messages and enquiries that do not lead to working together: at most 12 months after the last exchange, then we delete them. If the conversation becomes a contract, the contract documents are kept as long as the law requires.
priv.keep.p2: The counter that limits messages keeps your IP address for at most an hour after your last attempt, then deletes it.

Write to mail@konta.md: we answer within one working day.

We use them to answer you and, if you ask for a demo, to contact you about Konta. Without a name, an email address and a message we cannot answer you; the rest you give only if you want to. priv.what.p3: If you email or call us directly, we receive only what you tell or send us there.

sec.d1.h: Each company’s data kept apart by the database
sec.d1.p: Every table holding client data is protected by PostgreSQL’s row-level security. Someone without access to a company does not see its rows, even if the app gets it wrong. The app connects with a role that cannot bypass the rule, and a test fails if an unprotected table appears.
sec.d10.p: The app and the site send a Content Security Policy (CSP) that lets the browser run only their own scripts and does not let other sites frame their pages. Connections are HTTPS only.
sec.d2.p: The database refuses to change or delete entries, posted invoices and payments. Corrections are made only by reversal. Nothing enters a closed month, and reopening one needs a reason.
sec.d3.p: What changes in a company goes into a trail in which each row carries the fingerprint (hash) of the one before, so a row changed behind its back shows up when it is verified. The chain’s head is not yet published outside Konta; see below.
sec.d4.h: Support sees your books only with your consent
sec.d4.p: The director grants access, read-only and for a limited time, and can close it at any moment. The one exception, for emergencies, can be opened by the platform owner, with a written reason and for at most a day; it is recorded in the company’s trail and the directors get an email.
sec.d5.p: Anyone can confirm signing in with a code from an authenticator app or with a passkey, and whoever has turned it on uses it at every sign-in. A passkey also signs in without a password, since it proves both factors. Platform administrators cannot enter the console without a second factor.
sec.d6.p: Each secret is encrypted with its own key, and that key with a master key kept outside the database and its backups.
sec.d7.h: Lockout, and confirmation before sensitive changes
sec.d7.p: After too many wrong attempts, signing in to the account from that address is locked, and attempts from one address are limited. Before roles, statuses or access are changed, the app asks you to confirm again: with the second factor or, without one, with the password.
sec.d8.p: The sessions page shows where you are signed in and lets you end any session.
sec.d9.p: The app and the site load no analytics, no screen recording, no fonts and nothing else from other sites.
sec.l2.p: Somewhere not even we can rewrite, so that a trail rewritten from start to end would show.
sec.l3.p: Each client’s data encrypted with its own key.

sec.meta.description: How Konta keeps accounting data safe: what is done today and what we do before the first pilot client. Facts only, as of 1 November 2026.
sec.meta.title: Security · what is done and what comes next · Konta
sec.n1.p: Konta does not ask for or keep the password to Cabinetul personal, to MPass or to SIA e-Factura’s web interface. It signs in to no portal in your place.
sec.n2.p: Bank statements reach Konta as files the company downloads from its bank itself. Konta has no passwords, no codes and no connection to internet banking, and cannot send money from the company’s account.
sec.n3.p: Konta does not keep electronic signatures, USB tokens, mobile signatures or the PINs that unlock them. Once Konta sends invoices to e-Factura, it will send them unsigned, and the director will sign them in SIA e-Factura with their own signature.
sec.n4.h: The e-Factura API user, encrypted for each company
sec.n4.p: The only access of a company that Konta keeps is the API user the director creates in SIA e-Factura. It works only there and cannot sign invoices. Today Konta reads with it partners’ details by IDNO, the invoices the company issued and received, and an invoice’s PDF; it cancels an issued invoice there only when someone who may post asks, with a reason and after confirming who they are again. It sends no invoices. Only the director enters it, after confirming who they are again; the password is kept encrypted, tied to the company, and never shown to anyone again.
sec.n5.h: You can withdraw it without us
sec.n5.p: If you delete the API user in SIA e-Factura, Konta can no longer work in e-Factura for your company, from that moment on. You do not need to ask us for anything.
sec.n6.h: Every use, in the trail first
sec.n6.p: Before each request to e-Factura, Konta writes into the company’s trail what it is doing, what for and who asked for it; the password never goes there. A request that cannot be written into the trail is not made. The latest uses are shown on the company page.
sec.never.p: Konta does not hold SFS portal passwords, bank logins or qualified electronic signatures. It holds only access made for a program, which the issuer limits to one service and which the company can withdraw on its own. Only the director enters it, after confirming who they are again; it is kept encrypted, and every use goes into the company’s trail before it is made.
sec.p1: Facts only. Each line says whether it is done today or whether we do it before the first pilot client. Until everything on the second list is done, no real client data enters Konta.
sec.p1i.p: Each company’s e-Factura API user, kept encrypted, with every use in the company’s trail.
sec.p2i.h: A production server in the European Union
sec.p2i.p: Separate from today’s preview, and set up from nothing by a script.
sec.p3i.p: Encrypted before they leave the server and copied daily to Moldova, with no key there. A restore from that copy, rehearsed before the move to the production server.
sec.p4i.p: The books, documents and attachments as .xlsx and JSON, plus the original files.
sec.p5i.h: An email on a new sign-in
sec.p5i.p: A message when someone signs in to your account from a new device or address.
sec.p6i.h: Logs off the server, and alerts when it is down
sec.p6i.p: Operating logs shipped off the server, and an alert when the app stops answering.
sec.p7i.p: In every repository: automatic dependency updates are on; automatic scanning for secrets that slipped into the code and protection of the main branch come next.
sec.p8i.p: Carried out by an outside firm, with a second test after the fixes and no high or critical findings left.
sec.pilot.p: The conditions we set ourselves before a client’s real data enters Konta.
sec.report.p: Write to us at mail@konta.md. The address and the languages we answer in are also in the security.txt file, per RFC 9116.

vs.newBody: The new rate is already there when you open the program on Monday morning.

vs2.close.new: The database refuses any entry, reversal or opening balance in a closed month. Reopening it needs a reason and stays in the audit log.
vs2.close.old: There is a change-prohibition date, and anyone with the rights can move it.
vs2.close.q: The month is closed, and someone wants to change something in it.

vs2.fix.old: You open the document, correct it and post it again.
vs2.lead: Everything is built to make accountants’ work easier.

vs2.open.old: You save the trial balance, as you do at any month end.
vs2.open.q: You move a company into Konta.
vs2.pay.new: The cumulative method of HG 697/2014, with every rate, exemption and rounding rule taken from the public rulebook. You can run the same calculation in the salary calculator on this site.

cal.meta.description: Filing and payment deadlines at SFS, CNAS and CNAM, non-working days and changes in the law in Moldova, month by month, each with the legal act and article it comes from.
cal.title: The accountant's tax calendar
cal.filter.title: Show deadlines for
cal.months.label: Months
cal.changes.title: Changes in the law
cal.changes.lead: What has changed or will change in the tax rules: the date it applies from, the old and new value, and the act. A bill not yet adopted is marked as one.
cal.subscribe.title: Subscribe in your own calendar
cal.subscribe.lead: Copy a feed's address and add it as a subscription. Your calendar reads it again on its own, so a deadline that moves or a transferred day reaches it too.
cal.subscribe.google: Google Calendar: Other calendars, then From URL.
cal.subscribe.outlook: Outlook: Add calendar, then Subscribe from web.
cal.subscribe.apple: Calendar on iPhone or Mac: File, then New Calendar Subscription.
cal.method.title: How it is made
cal.method.p1: Nothing in this calendar is typed by hand. The deadlines, non-working days and changes in the law are data in the public konta-rulebook register, each with its legal act, article and where it was published. The page and the feeds are generated from it.
cal.method.p2: When a tax deadline falls on a rest day or a public holiday, we move it to the next working day, as the Fiscal Code requires in art. 129 item 8), and check the date against the one SFS or CNAS published. The deadlines of NBS, of the financial statements and of CNAM's fixed premium are not tax obligations: when one falls on a non-working day we say so next to it, without moving it. Public holidays are those of the Labour Code, art. 111; a locality's patron saint's day is not shown, as it is a day off only there.
cal.method.p3: A deadline we found only in secondary sources is not shown with a date. It stays under "Deadlines we do not show yet" until we have read it in the act.
cal.method.p4: The calendar shows the general obligations. A company may have others, depending on its activity, its regime or an authority's decision, and statistical reports are filed only by the units the National Bureau of Statistics has included in a survey.
cal.moved: {date} is not a working day ({why}), so the deadline moves to the next working day. Legal basis:

cal.empty: No dates to keep in mind this month.
cal.transfers.unknown: For {year} the Government has not yet published the transfer of rest days. Public holidays are those of the Labour Code; a later decision may move days.
cal.nextyear: The {year} deadlines are computed from the law in force today; acts adopted for {year} may change them.
cal.dirty: With changes not yet published in the register.

sal.meta.title: Salary calculator 2026: from gross to net · Konta
sal.meta.description: From the gross salary, what the employee receives and what the employer pays for a month in 2026: the medical premium, the exemptions, income tax, the social contribution. Every value from the public rulebook, with its act.
sal.title: Salary calculator 2026
sal.lead: From the gross salary, what the employee receives and what the employer pays for a month in 2026. Every value comes from the public rulebook that the Konta app computes from too, with the act it is taken from.
sal.review: The values are still being checked by a licensed accountant.
sal.gross.error: Write the amount in MDL in figures, with at most two decimals.
sal.personal: The employee has asked for the personal exemption
sal.noscript: Without JavaScript, the result beside stays the example of MDL {out:gross} with the personal exemption.
sal.caption: One month, in MDL
sal.out.net: Net salary, received by the employee
sal.capped: Twelve months at this salary exceed the annual ceiling of MDL {amount:cap}, so the personal exemption is not due and has not been deducted.
sal.how.p1: The calculator computes one month of a year in which the employee is paid the same salary every month from January, by one employer, with no other income. The medical insurance premium is withheld from the gross salary. The exemptions are taken off what remains: the personal exemption, MDL {amount:personalMonth} a month, if the employee asked for it, and MDL {amount:dependantMonth} a month for each dependant. The result is the taxable income, from which income tax is withheld. On top of the salary, the employer pays the social insurance contribution, computed on the gross salary.
sal.how.p2: The tax is computed cumulatively from the start of the year, as Government Decision 697/2014 requires; with the same salary every month, every month comes out the same. Every amount is rounded to the ban, and half a ban is rounded up.
sal.how.p3: The personal exemption is not granted to a person whose taxable income for the year exceeds MDL {amount:cap}. The calculator takes it off only if twelve months at the salary entered do not exceed that amount, that is up to MDL {amount:capMonth} a month. The Fiscal Code counts income from every source, and whoever exceeds the ceiling settles it in the annual return.
sal.check.p1: The calculator on this page and the payroll in the Konta app are two separate programs. Both pass the same {count:cases} examples, {count:months} months in all, from one public file in the rulebook. The first is the example SFS publishes, the one beside: gross {out:gross}, premium {out:medical}, exemption {out:exemption}, taxable income {out:taxable}, tax {out:incomeTax}, net {out:net}.
sal.check.p2: If the two differed, even by one ban, the page would not be published. Amounts are counted in whole bani, never in floating-point numbers.
sal.not.1: Only one month, with the same salary all year: not the whole year, months with different salaries, days worked, leave or benefits.
sal.not.2: No major personal exemption, no exemption for a spouse, and no higher amount for a dependant with a disability.
sal.not.3: Only the general rate of the social insurance contribution, {rate:cnas}: no other categories of insured people and no minimum or maximum base.
sal.not.4: It sees only this salary. The employee’s other income, which counts for the personal exemption’s ceiling, is unknown to it.
sal.not.5: No salary advances, bonuses or other payments beyond the monthly salary.
sal.not.6: It does not replace the payroll the accountant makes.
sal.v.cnam: Medical insurance premium, withheld from the employee
sal.v.cnas: Social insurance contribution, paid by the employer
sal.v.cap: Annual income ceiling for the personal exemption
sal.v.dependant: Exemption for one dependant, a year
sal.v.premium: The medical premium is deducted before tax
sal.v.round.act: Our choice: the acts read give no rounding rule.
sal.values.note: The values are those of the md-2026 set in the public konta-rulebook, read when the page was published. A licensed accountant is checking them now and has not approved them yet. You can check them yourself, line by line, each with the act it comes from.
guide.meta.title: The Konta guide for accountants · Konta
guide.meta.description: Step by step, how to work in Konta today: the e-Factura API user, opening balances from 1C, the first month, closing the month and importing a bank statement.
guide.title: The Konta guide for accountants
guide.lead: How to work in Konta, step by step, as the app is today. Konta is still in development: the app at demo.konta.md is the demo. The guide grows with every new feature.
guide.ef.h: How to create the e-Factura API user
guide.ef.p1: An accounting program works with SIA e-Factura through an API user that the company creates, not with your SFS password. The director enters it in Konta on the Company page, after confirming who they are again. Konta keeps it encrypted and reads the company’s issued and received invoices with it, and every use appears in the company’s trail. Invoices are not sent through Konta yet: issuing is in progress.
guide.ef.s1: Only someone with the company’s manager role in SIA e-Factura can create the API user, usually the director.
guide.ef.s2: Sign in to SIA e-Factura through MPass, with the electronic signature.
guide.ef.s3: Open Setări (Settings), then Utilizatorii companiei (Company users).
guide.ef.s4: Press Creați utilizator API (Create API user), fill in the fields and save.
guide.ef.s5: Keep the user’s name and password somewhere safe, and do not send them by email.
guide.ef.n1: We went through these steps on 8 October 2026 on SFS’s test portal, preproductie.sfs.md: the director signed in with the electronic signature and created the API user under Setări, Utilizatorii companiei. SFS’s integration guide describes the same steps.
guide.ef.n2: According to SFS’s guide, the API user has access to every function of the platform, so it has to be kept like a key. Signing invoices stays with a person, in the SIA e-Factura interface.
guide.open.p1: Konta does not read the 1C database. It starts from the closing balances in the trial balance of the last month kept in 1C.
guide.open.s1: In 1C, run the trial balance for the last month, with subaccounts, and save it as .xlsx or .csv. An old .xls file is first saved as .xlsx from Excel.
guide.open.s2: In Konta, open Opening balances and choose the balances’ date: the start of the day you work in Konta from, usually 1 January.
guide.open.s3: Upload the file or paste the cells copied from Excel. Konta picks the closing balance columns, the last debit and credit pair in a 1C trial balance; you can change them.
guide.open.s4: Check the table. Every problem shows on its own row: an account that is not in the chart of accounts, a negative amount, a balance on both the debit and the credit side. An account listed together with its own subaccounts is set aside, and if its total does not equal the sum of its subaccounts, Konta says so.
guide.open.s5: Press Post the opening balances. They go in once, as the “Opening balances” entry in the Journal, and the Trial balance shows them as the opening balance.
guide.open.n1: To replace them, reverse the “Opening balances” entry in the Journal and load them again. The file is checked by the antivirus before it is read, and amounts are read exactly as written in the cells.
guide.first.p1: After the opening balances, the month is kept from documents. What can be done in the app today:
guide.first.s1: Company: the company details printed on documents and returns, such as the name, the addresses, the bank account and the codes. Only the director can change them.
guide.first.s2: Partners: customers and suppliers. When you type an IDNO, Konta can offer the partner’s details from SFS, from its test service for now: the official name, the address, the VAT code and the registered accounts. You take them only if you choose them.
guide.first.s3: Sales invoices: an invoice is made as a draft and posted. When posted it gets the next number, with no gaps, and the receivable, the revenue and the VAT go into the books. A posted invoice is cancelled only by reversal.
guide.first.s4: Purchase invoices: with the supplier’s series and number. Each line is posted to its own account, deductible VAT to 534, the supplier to 521.
guide.first.s5: Receipts and payments: a payment settles the partner’s posted invoices, exactly its amount, and an advance received or paid is settled against invoices later.
guide.first.s6: Payroll, for the director, the chief accountant and payroll staff: the employees, with the salary from hiring and its changes, then the month’s payroll, computed by the cumulative method, with timesheets and leave. It is posted, then paid. Months are posted in order.
guide.first.s7: VAT registers: sales and purchases by rate, with the VAT payable or to recover. TVA12 is filled in from them; the return’s form is not in Konta yet.
guide.first.s8: Journal, Trial balance, Account statement and General ledger: a manual entry for what does not come from documents, and the reports to check with.
guide.first.s9: Cash: receipt and payment orders and the day’s cash book.
guide.first.s10: Acts of completed works: the act with its invoice or on its own. Proforma invoices: an offer that stays out of the books and becomes, on request, a draft invoice.
guide.first.s11: Fixed assets, Stock, Share capital, Credits and loans (under Receipts and payments) and Prepaid expenses (under Purchase invoices): each with its own documents; a posted document is cancelled by reversal.
guide.first.n1: Not in Konta yet: the TVA12, IPC21 and VEN12 returns, financial statements and issuing invoices through e-Factura.
guide.close.p1: Closing locks the month: after it, no entry, reversal or opening balance goes in with a date in the closed period. The database does the locking, not only the app.
guide.close.s1: Open Period close. For the month chosen, the screen shows its steps, those that apply: fixed asset depreciation, payroll, the month’s VAT statement for a VAT payer, loan interest, prepaid expenses and, recommended, the revaluation of balances in a currency.
guide.close.s2: Do each step. The checks under the steps block nothing, but show what is worth a look: the registers against their accounts, entries posted by hand, drafts left in the month.
guide.close.s3: Press Close the period. Only the chief accountant can close, and only once the required steps are done.
guide.close.s4: If something has to be corrected, Reopen moves the closing date back. It asks for a reason and for confirmation that it is you, and the reason stays in the history and in the audit trail.
guide.close.n1: Closing the year is on the same page: once the year has ended, the chief accountant posts on its last day income and expenses into 351 and the result into 333.
guide.bank.p1: Konta does not connect to your bank and does not ask for your bank login. You download the statement from your bank and upload it to Konta.
guide.bank.s1: Open Receipts and payments, then Bank statements.
guide.bank.s2: Choose the format: MT940, or a CSV or Excel table. Each bank’s own format will come once we have real statements from it.
guide.bank.s3: For a table, say once what each column holds: the date and how it is written, the amount (one column with a minus for money out, or two columns, in and out) and, where there are any, the document number, the counterparty, the fiscal code, the IBAN and the payment’s purpose. The columns are kept for the company.
guide.bank.s4: Upload the file. It is checked by the antivirus, then read line by line. An MT940 statement whose opening balance and movements do not make its closing balance is refused whole.
guide.bank.s5: A line that names a partner, by IDNO or by IBAN, and its invoices, by the number in the payment’s purpose or as the one open invoice for exactly that amount, becomes a draft payment. Nothing is posted on its own: check the draft and press Post the payment.
guide.bank.s6: For a line left to resolve, choose the partner and the invoices, or set it aside with a reason, for example a bank fee posted in the journal.
guide.bank.n1: A line that an earlier, overlapping statement already brought is recognised and does not become a second payment, and the same file is not imported twice. A statement may be in a foreign currency too.
guide.outro: If a step here is no longer true in the app, it is a mistake. Write to us and we will correct it.
